figures.shows: Herschel/PACS 70 µm image of the Helix Nebula with a zoom-in grid of four cutaway panels centred on WD 2226-210, comparing Spitzer 24 µm, SOFIA HAWC+ 54 µm, Herschel 70 µm and ALMA Band 6 imaging of the white dwarf region; only Spitzer and Herschel detect excess emission at the white dwarf.
readable_values: approx. 70 µm colour scale spans -2.0 to 1.0 mJy/arcsec^2
approx. Spitzer 24 µm panel colour scale spans 1.0 to 1.5 mJy/arcsec^2
approx. Herschel 70 µm zoom colour scale spans 0 to 0.5 mJy/arcsec^2
approx. HAWC+ and ALMA panel colour scales span -2 to 2 mJy/arcsec^2
figures.caption_quote: Only the Spitzer and Herschel observations detect the excess emission associated with the white dwarf.

figures.shows: Herschel/PACS 70 µm imaging of the white dwarf region showing the two-component decomposition: the original map, the fitted 2D Gaussian extended component, its residual, the compact PSF-matched Gaussian, and the final residual with the extended and compact component footprints overlaid.
figures.validation_check: Shows the residual after subtracting the fitted extended and compact Gaussian components, testing whether the central 70 µm emission is separated into components.
readable_values: approx. colour scale of data maps 0 to 1.0 mJy/pixel
approx. extended-component ellipse FWHM 28 by 24 arcsec
approx. compact component FWHM 5.4 arcsec
figures.caption_quote: The shaded ellipses in this panel denote the extent of the extended (FWHM 28′′ × 24′′, φ 65◦) and compact (FWHM 5.4′′) components subtracted from the image.

figures.shows: Spectral energy distribution of the central source WD 2226-210 from optical to millimetre wavelengths, with the white dwarf photosphere model, the compact and extended modified blackbody dust components, and their model realisations drawn from the tested parameter ranges.
figures.validation_check: Model fit to photometry and upper limits for the compact and extended dust components, showing which parameter ranges are consistent with the observations.
readable_values: approx. peak white dwarf photosphere flux about 1000 mJy near 0.05 µm
approx. compact component peak about 50 mJy near 30 µm
approx. extended component peak about 200 mJy near 100 µm
figures.caption_quote: The black solid line denotes the white dwarf photopshere model scaled to optical and near-infrared photometry, shown as grey circles.

figures.shows: Comparison of observed photometry with model SEDs for four debris-disc scenarios (A to D) differing in dust radius and grain size range, showing that only scenario A with small minimum grain size matches all observations.
figures.validation_check: Tests whether each grain-size and disc-architecture scenario reproduces the mid-infrared rise and far-infrared and millimetre constraints, favouring a small minimum grain size.
readable_values: approx. Model A far-infrared peak about 30 mJy near 30 µm
approx. Model A 24 µm data point about 50 mJy
approx. Model B and C peak values near 50 to 80 mJy
approx. 3-sigma upper limit at 1.3 mm about 0.2 mJy
figures.caption_quote: Of the four scenarios considered here, only scenario A, with a small minimum grain size and narrow size distribution is consistent with all the observations.
